study_type_evidence.quote: The mice were intraperitoneally injected with 50 μg/kg IFN-1CTPON, IFN-2CTPON, or rhIFN-α2b.
The traditional WISH/VSV system was used to evaluate the antiviral activities of the IFNs.

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: male BALB/c, body weight 18 ± 2 g; age not reported
in_vivo_species.quote: Male BALB/c mice (weight 18 ± 2 g) were purchased from Beijing Huafukang Bioscience Co., Inc.

in_vitro_detail: WISH cell / vesicular stomatitis virus cytopathic-effect antiviral assay; HeLa cell antiproliferation assay (CellTiter 96 AQueous); HepG2.2.15 anti-HBV assay with HBsAg ELISA; CHO DG44 expression, MTX clone selection, dot blot, Western blot and PNGase F deglycosylation.

agents.name: IFN-1CTPON (rhIFN-α2b fused at the C-terminus with CTP plus an N-glycosylation sequence)
agents.sequence: CTP moiety reported as SSSSKAPPPSLPSPSRLPGPSDTPILPQ with C-terminal-linked N-glycosylation sequence NGTV; the rhIFN-α2b portion sequence is not printed in the body
agents.sequence_source: METHODS (Expression vector construction and CHO cell transformation): 'The 28-amino-acid (SSSSKAPPPSLPSPSRLPGPSDTPILPQ) CTP sequence and the C-terminal-linked N-glycosylation sequence (NGTV)'
agents.chemical_identifier: Expressed from plasmid pEE12.4-IFN-1CTPON in CHO DG44 cells; apparent MW 22 kDa by Western blot; purity >99%
agents.group_n_quote: Mice were randomly divided into three groups, with eight in each group.
agents.route: intraperitoneal per Methods; the Results section instead describes the administration as subcutaneous
agents.dose_route_quote: The mice were intraperitoneally injected with 50 μg/kg IFN-1CTPON, IFN-2CTPON, or rhIFN-α2b.
agents.half_life_matrix: mouse blood/serum (intraocular venous blood, IFN measured by ELISA)
agents.pk_section: Table 1 (Pharmacokinetic parameters in mice calculated with WinNonLin)

agents.name: IFN-2CTPON (rhIFN-α2b fused with CTP plus N-glycosylation sequence at both the N- and C-termini)
agents.sequence: CTP moiety reported as SSSSKAPPPSLPSPSRLPGPSDTPILPQ with linked N-glycosylation sequence NGTV, fused at both termini; the rhIFN-α2b portion sequence is not printed in the body
agents.sequence_source: METHODS (Expression vector construction and CHO cell transformation) and RESULTS: 'CTPON was fused to IFN-α2b at the C-terminus or at both termini'
agents.chemical_identifier: Expressed from plasmid pEE12.4-IFN-2CTPON in CHO DG44 cells; apparent MW 25 kDa by Western blot; purity >97%
agents.group_n_quote: Mice were randomly divided into three groups, with eight in each group.
agents.route: intraperitoneal per Methods; the Results section instead describes the administration as subcutaneous
agents.dose_route_quote: The mice were intraperitoneally injected with 50 μg/kg IFN-1CTPON, IFN-2CTPON, or rhIFN-α2b.
agents.half_life_matrix: mouse blood/serum (intraocular venous blood, IFN measured by ELISA)
agents.pk_quote: The half-life of IFN-2CTPON was 3.45 h, which was longer than that of IFN-1CTPON (2.62 h) or rhIFN-α2b (1.34 h).

agents.sequence_source: No amino-acid sequence of rhIFN-α2b is printed in the body.
agents.chemical_identifier: rhIFN-α2b obtained from Yuan-Ce Corporation (Beijing, China); also used as the IFN activity standard (1000 U/ml) in the WISH/VSV assay

concentration_time_figure.note: No figure plotting blood/serum concentration against time is present. Pharmacokinetic results are given only as a parameter table (Table 1); Figure 4 plots in vitro antiproliferative and anti-HBV activity versus concentration, not concentration versus time.

bioanalytical_method: ELISA. The half-life study used an ELISA kit (Abcam) to measure IFN concentrations; expression/purification quantification used the Human IFN-α (subtype 2) ELISA development kit (3423-1H-6, MabTech). PK parameters were fitted with WinNonLin.
bioanalytical_quote: Intraocular venous blood was collected at 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, and 24 h postinjection. The IFN concentration was determined with an ELISA kit (Abcam).
notes: ROUTE DISCREPANCY: the Methods state the mice were injected intraperitoneally ('The mice were intraperitoneally injected with 50 μg/kg'), while the Results state 'The pharmacokinetic profiles of the subcutaneously administered IFN-1CTPON and IFN-2CTPON in mice'. Both statements are recorded; the route is therefore not unambiguously established by the body. Full PK parameters for all three agents at 50 μg/kg are in Table 1 (T1/2, Tmax, Cmax, AUC). AUC values: 59.21 ± 21.01 (IFN-1CTPON), 254.67 ± 69.58 (IFN-2CTPON) and 39.87 ± 11.9 ng·h/ml (rhIFN-α2b). Only the 28-residue CTP sequence (SSSSKAPPPSLPSPSRLPGPSDTPILPQ) and the N-glycosylation sequence (NGTV) are printed in the body; the rhIFN-α2b backbone sequence is not, so the full fusion-protein sequences cannot be reconstructed from the body. Sampling times were 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 24 h; investigators were blinded to group allocation. No vehicle-only or untreated control arm is described for the PK study.
